objective: Compare search from raw Boolean actions versus the same algorithm with an optional previously learned crossing on an independently defined ternary relation. Measure held-out success, censored candidate counts, expanded primitive work and acquisition break-even across five paired seeds.
status: Across five paired seeds both arms sampled an exact program, yet every training-selected checkpoint held 3/9. Reuse averaged 260 fewer proposals to the first exact sample and consumed 27.63% more expanded gates. No compute payback observed.
title: Cost of reusing a frozen crossing on a new three-label task
